doc.title: Tommy Newsom and Ross Tompkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Acoustic jazz may return
summary: Tommy says the business will change and machines cannot replicate players like Snooky Young, Sweets Edison, Roy Eldridge.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: My own encouragement I could give to people is that things don’t stay the same, and the condition that the music business is in right now might change.
It keeps going around, you know.

If acoustic stays out long enough, it might be the new thing in a while, you know, if people get enough of digitally produced sounds, they might—if they hear guys, like hear Snooky Young play. Or Sweets Edison. Did you happen to hear him play?
We talked to him. We didn’t get to hear him.
Well he has a way of playing. I don’t think a machine could ever do that.
Oh, no, you know who that is, there’s no doubt about that. It can’t be done electrically. Or Roy Eldridge. Remember I was playing you that tape the other night? You can’t duplicate that.
Of course old timers always say that.
I do too. And nothing stays the same, so they shouldn’t despair.
